name_note: GTDB divides the classical genus Eubacterium into several genera, of which g__Eubacterium_R is one, so literature on Eubacterium covers a broader group than this GTDB genus.

sentences.text: Eubacterium is a phylogenetically and phenotypically diverse genus of gut bacteria whose members form part of the core human gut microbiome.
A review describes several members of the genus as butyrate producers, and butyrate as important for energy homeostasis, colonic motility, immunomodulation and suppression of inflammation in the gut.
The same review reports that Eubacterium species carry out bile acid and cholesterol transformations in the gut.
That review also states that gut dysbiosis and a modified representation of Eubacterium species have been linked with various human disease states.
A study of human primary gastrointestinal B cell lymphomas reported a microbiota profile with decreased symbiotic microbes, particularly the genus Eubacterium.
